summary.text: For \(n=9\), the primorial is \(2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\cdot19\cdot23=223092870\), and its square plus one is \(49770428644836901=29^2\cdot59180057841661\). Hence this term is not squarefree, so the conjunction fails regardless of the infinitude claim.

full_proof.text:
Let the primes in increasing order be
\[
p_0=2,\quad p_1=3,\quad p_2=5,\quad p_3=7,\ldots,
\]
and define
\[
P_n=\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}p_k,
\qquad
a(n)=P_n^2+1.
\]
Thus the empty product gives \(a(0)=2\), in agreement with the indexing of the sequence.

We disprove the assertion that every \(a(n)\) is squarefree by considering \(n=9\). The first nine primes are
\[
2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23.
\]
Their product is
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_9
 &=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\cdot19\cdot23\\
 &=223092870.
\end{aligned}
\]
For completeness, this product can be obtained successively as
\[
2,\ 6,\ 30,\ 210,\ 2310,\ 30030,\ 510510,\ 9699690,\ 223092870.
\]

We now reduce this primorial modulo \(29^2\). Since \(29^2=841\), direct division gives
\[
223092870=841\cdot265271-41.
\]
Consequently,
\[
P_9\equiv -41\pmod{841}.
\]
Squaring and adding one yields
\[
a(9)=P_9^2+1\equiv (-41)^2+1=1682=2\cdot841\equiv0\pmod{841}.
\]
Therefore
\[
29^2=841\mid a(9).
\]
This divisibility can also be displayed as an exact identity. Expanding the preceding expression for \(P_9\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(9)
  &=(841\cdot265271-41)^2+1\\
  &=841\bigl(841\cdot265271^2-82\cdot265271+2\bigr)\\
  &=841\cdot59180057841661.
\end{aligned}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
a(9)=223092870^2+1=49770428644836901
      =29^2\cdot59180057841661.
\]

The number \(29\) is prime: any composite divisorization of \(29\) would have a prime divisor at most \(\sqrt{29}<6\), hence one of \(2,3,5\), but \(29\) is divisible by none of these. Thus the displayed divisibility says that the square of a prime divides \(a(9)\).

A positive integer is squarefree precisely when no square of a prime divides it. Since \(29^2\mid a(9)\), the term \(a(9)\) is not squarefree. Hence the universal assertion
\[
\forall n\in\mathbb N,\quad a(n)\text{ is squarefree}
\]
is false.

The conjecture under consideration is the conjunction of this universal squarefreeness assertion with the assertion that \(a(n)\) is prime for infinitely many \(n\). A conjunction is false as soon as either of its two components is false. The counterexample \(n=9\) disproves its first component, irrespective of whether the second component is true or false. Therefore the combined conjecture is false.
